A **half marathon** is a [road running](link_6) event of 21.0975 kilometres (c. 13 mi 192.5 yd)—half the distance of a [marathon](link_7).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-1) It is common for a half marathon event to be held concurrently with a marathon or a 5K race, using almost the same course with a late start, an early finish, or shortcuts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-2)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] If finisher medals are awarded, the medal or ribbon may differ from those for the full marathon. The half marathon is also known by its [rounded](link_8) distance: a _21K_, a _21.1K_, or _**13.1** miles_.

A [half marathon world record](link_9) is officially recognised by [World Athletics](link_10).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_men_record-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_women_record-4) The men's world record time is 56:51, set by [Yomif Kejelcha](link_2) in 2026 in [Buenos Aires](link_11). [Jacob Kiplimo](link_12) ran 56:42 in [Barcelona](link_13) in 2025, but this mark was not ratified by World Athletics due to his proximity to the lead car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-5) The women's world record, in a mixed-gender race, is 1:02:52, set by [Letesenbet Gidey](link_4) of Ethiopia in October 2021 in [Valencia, Spain](link_14). The world record for the women's only race is 1:05:15, set by [Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5) of Kenya in September 2026.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-6)

Participation in half marathons has grown steadily since 2003,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) partly because it is a challenging distance, but does not require the same level of training that a marathon does.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) In 2008, _Running USA_ reported that the half marathon was the fastest-growing type of race.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7)

Races close to the official half marathon distance of 21.0975 km (13.1094 mi) have taken place throughout the early 20th century, and athletes have also been timed at the midpoint of full [marathons](link_7). The [1946 Central American and Caribbean Games](link_15) in [Barranquilla](link_16), Colombia featured a road race that is listed at exactly the modern half marathon distance, referred to as the "Carrera Centroamericana y del Caribe: (21 kms. 97,5 metros)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-8) The [1952 South American Championships in Athletics](link_17) in [Buenos Aires](link_11), Argentina featured a road race that was 21.097km, referred to as "la media maratón" ('the half marathon') by the Chilean newspaper _La Nación._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-9)

The earliest half marathon recognised by the [ARRS](link_18) is the 1960 [Romford](link_19) Half Marathon in England, though it was short of the full half marathon distance.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-10) The earliest half marathon recognised by [World Athletics](link_10) is the 1965 [Feckleton Half Marathon](link_20) in England. The event grew in popularity, leading to the eventual establishment of the [World Athletics Road Running Championships](link_21) in 1992, originally titled the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships.

Click here for more information.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Featured_lists "This is a featured list. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics "1896 Summer Olympics") (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic")) and [Olympic records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_record "Olympic record") are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)") events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_field "Track and field") (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_field "Track and field") (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics"), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Johnson_(Canadian_sprinter) "Ben Johnson (Canadian sprinter)") broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_metres "100 metres") sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabolic_steroid "Anabolic steroid") to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Lewis "Carl Lewis").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%B3bert_Fazekas "Róbert Fazekas") broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Beamon "Bob Beamon")'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics "1968 Summer Olympics").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Powell_(athlete) "Mike Powell (athlete)"), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1991 World Championships in Athletics") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

No longer contested at the Summer Olympics

[![Image 3: Usain Bolt in a yellow running vest and green shorts just completing a race](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg/250px-Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg)

[Usain Bolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usain_Bolt "Usain Bolt") currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_metres "100 metres")&[200 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/200_metres "200 metres"), and one with the [Jamaican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Jamaica at the 2008 Summer Olympics")[4 × 100 m relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_%C3%97_100_metres_relay "4 × 100 metres relay") team.

Ethiopian long-distance runner [Kenenisa Bekele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele "Kenenisa Bekele") holds the Olympic record in the 5000 m.

Russian athlete [Yelena Isinbayeva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yelena_Isinbayeva "Yelena Isinbayeva") set the Olympic record in the pole vault in Beijing in 2008.

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

A **half marathon** is a [road running](link_6) event of 21.0975 kilometres (c. 13 mi 192.5 yd)—half the distance of a [marathon](link_7).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-1) It is common for a half marathon event to be held concurrently with a marathon or a 5K race, using almost the same course with a late start, an early finish, or shortcuts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-2)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] If finisher medals are awarded, the medal or ribbon may differ from those for the full marathon. The half marathon is also known by its [rounded](link_8) distance: a _21K_, a _21.1K_, or _**13.1** miles_.

A [half marathon world record](link_9) is officially recognised by [World Athletics](link_10).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_men_record-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_women_record-4) The men's world record time is 56:51, set by [Yomif Kejelcha](link_2) in 2026 in [Buenos Aires](link_11). [Jacob Kiplimo](link_12) ran 56:42 in [Barcelona](link_13) in 2025, but this mark was not ratified by World Athletics due to his proximity to the lead car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-5) The women's world record, in a mixed-gender race, is 1:02:52, set by [Letesenbet Gidey](link_4) of Ethiopia in October 2021 in [Valencia, Spain](link_14). The world record for the women's only race is 1:05:15, set by [Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5) of Kenya in September 2026.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-6)

Participation in half marathons has grown steadily since 2003,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) partly because it is a challenging distance, but does not require the same level of training that a marathon does.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) In 2008, _Running USA_ reported that the half marathon was the fastest-growing type of race.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7)

Races close to the official half marathon distance of 21.0975 km (13.1094 mi) have taken place throughout the early 20th century, and athletes have also been timed at the midpoint of full [marathons](link_7). The [1946 Central American and Caribbean Games](link_15) in [Barranquilla](link_16), Colombia featured a road race that is listed at exactly the modern half marathon distance, referred to as the "Carrera Centroamericana y del Caribe: (21 kms. 97,5 metros)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-8) The [1952 South American Championships in Athletics](link_17) in [Buenos Aires](link_11), Argentina featured a road race that was 21.097km, referred to as "la media maratón" ('the half marathon') by the Chilean newspaper _La Nación._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-9)

The earliest half marathon recognised by the [ARRS](link_18) is the 1960 [Romford](link_19) Half Marathon in England, though it was short of the full half marathon distance.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-10) The earliest half marathon recognised by [World Athletics](link_10) is the 1965 [Feckleton Half Marathon](link_20) in England. The event grew in popularity, leading to the eventual establishment of the [World Athletics Road Running Championships](link_21) in 1992, originally titled the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

No longer contested at the Summer Olympics

[![Image 3: Usain Bolt in a yellow running vest and green shorts just completing a race](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg/250px-Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg)

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg)

Ethiopian long-distance runner [Kenenisa Bekele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele "Kenenisa Bekele") holds the Olympic record in the 5000 m.

_♦ denotes a performance that is also a current [world record](link_24). Statistics are correct as of August 5, 2024._

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg/250px-Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg)

Russian athlete [Yelena Isinbayeva](link_25) set the Olympic record in the pole vault in Beijing in 2008.

| [World records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics#World_records "List of world records in athletics") |
| Men | ![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg/40px-Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Yomif Kejelcha](link_2)(ETH) 56:51 (2026) |
| Women | **[Mx](link_3)**: ![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg/40px-Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Letesenbet Gidey](link_4)(ETH) 1:02:52 (2021) **[Wo](link_3)**: ![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Flag_of_Kenya.svg/40px-Flag_of_Kenya.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5)(KEN) 1:05:15 (2026) |

A **half marathon** is a [road running](link_6) event of 21.0975 kilometres (c. 13 mi 192.5 yd)—half the distance of a [marathon](link_7).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-1) It is common for a half marathon event to be held concurrently with a marathon or a 5K race, using almost the same course with a late start, an early finish, or shortcuts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-2)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] If finisher medals are awarded, the medal or ribbon may differ from those for the full marathon. The half marathon is also known by its [rounded](link_8) distance: a _21K_, a _21.1K_, or _**13.1** miles_.

A [half marathon world record](link_9) is officially recognised by [World Athletics](link_10).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_men_record-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_women_record-4) The men's world record time is 56:51, set by [Yomif Kejelcha](link_2) in 2026 in [Buenos Aires](link_11). [Jacob Kiplimo](link_12) ran 56:42 in [Barcelona](link_13) in 2025, but this mark was not ratified by World Athletics due to his proximity to the lead car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-5) The women's world record, in a mixed-gender race, is 1:02:52, set by [Letesenbet Gidey](link_4) of Ethiopia in October 2021 in [Valencia, Spain](link_14). The world record for the women's only race is 1:05:15, set by [Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5) of Kenya in September 2026.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-6)

Participation in half marathons has grown steadily since 2003,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) partly because it is a challenging distance, but does not require the same level of training that a marathon does.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) In 2008, _Running USA_ reported that the half marathon was the fastest-growing type of race.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7)

Races close to the official half marathon distance of 21.0975 km (13.1094 mi) have taken place throughout the early 20th century, and athletes have also been timed at the midpoint of full [marathons](link_7). The [1946 Central American and Caribbean Games](link_15) in [Barranquilla](link_16), Colombia featured a road race that is listed at exactly the modern half marathon distance, referred to as the "Carrera Centroamericana y del Caribe: (21 kms. 97,5 metros)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-8) The [1952 South American Championships in Athletics](link_17) in [Buenos Aires](link_11), Argentina featured a road race that was 21.097km, referred to as "la media maratón" ('the half marathon') by the Chilean newspaper _La Nación._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-9)

The earliest half marathon recognised by the [ARRS](link_18) is the 1960 [Romford](link_19) Half Marathon in England, though it was short of the full half marathon distance.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-10) The earliest half marathon recognised by [World Athletics](link_10) is the 1965 [Feckleton Half Marathon](link_20) in England. The event grew in popularity, leading to the eventual establishment of the [World Athletics Road Running Championships](link_21) in 1992, originally titled the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships.

*   Updated 23 August 2026.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-12)

The **18th [European Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Athletics_Championships "European Athletics Championships")** were held from 6 August to 11 August 2002 in the [Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Munich) "Olympic Stadium (Munich)") of [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany").

The **18th [European Athletics Championships](link_7)** were held from 6 August to 11 August 2002 in the [Olympic Stadium](link_4) of [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"), [Germany](link_3).

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

A **half marathon** is a [road running](link_6) event of 21.0975 kilometres (c. 13 mi 192.5 yd)—half the distance of a [marathon](link_7).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-1) It is common for a half marathon event to be held concurrently with a marathon or a 5K race, using almost the same course with a late start, an early finish, or shortcuts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-2)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] If finisher medals are awarded, the medal or ribbon may differ from those for the full marathon. The half marathon is also known by its [rounded](link_8) distance: a _21K_, a _21.1K_, or _**13.1** miles_.

A [half marathon world record](link_9) is officially recognised by [World Athletics](link_10).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_men_record-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_women_record-4) The men's world record time is 56:51, set by [Yomif Kejelcha](link_2) in 2026 in [Buenos Aires](link_11). [Jacob Kiplimo](link_12) ran 56:42 in [Barcelona](link_13) in 2025, but this mark was not ratified by World Athletics due to his proximity to the lead car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-5) The women's world record, in a mixed-gender race, is 1:02:52, set by [Letesenbet Gidey](link_4) of Ethiopia in October 2021 in [Valencia, Spain](link_14). The world record for the women's only race is 1:05:15, set by [Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5) of Kenya in September 2026.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-6)

Participation in half marathons has grown steadily since 2003,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) partly because it is a challenging distance, but does not require the same level of training that a marathon does.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) In 2008, _Running USA_ reported that the half marathon was the fastest-growing type of race.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7)

Races close to the official half marathon distance of 21.0975 km (13.1094 mi) have taken place throughout the early 20th century, and athletes have also been timed at the midpoint of full [marathons](link_7). The [1946 Central American and Caribbean Games](link_15) in [Barranquilla](link_16), Colombia featured a road race that is listed at exactly the modern half marathon distance, referred to as the "Carrera Centroamericana y del Caribe: (21 kms. 97,5 metros)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-8) The [1952 South American Championships in Athletics](link_17) in [Buenos Aires](link_11), Argentina featured a road race that was 21.097km, referred to as "la media maratón" ('the half marathon') by the Chilean newspaper _La Nación._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-9)

The earliest half marathon recognised by the [ARRS](link_18) is the 1960 [Romford](link_19) Half Marathon in England, though it was short of the full half marathon distance.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-10) The earliest half marathon recognised by [World Athletics](link_10) is the 1965 [Feckleton Half Marathon](link_20) in England. The event grew in popularity, leading to the eventual establishment of the [World Athletics Road Running Championships](link_21) in 1992, originally titled the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

No longer contested at the Summer Olympics

[![Image 3: Usain Bolt in a yellow running vest and green shorts just completing a race](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg/250px-Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg)

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

A **half marathon** is a [road running](link_6) event of 21.0975 kilometres (c. 13 mi 192.5 yd)—half the distance of a [marathon](link_7).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-1) It is common for a half marathon event to be held concurrently with a marathon or a 5K race, using almost the same course with a late start, an early finish, or shortcuts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-2)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] If finisher medals are awarded, the medal or ribbon may differ from those for the full marathon. The half marathon is also known by its [rounded](link_8) distance: a _21K_, a _21.1K_, or _**13.1** miles_.

A [half marathon world record](link_9) is officially recognised by [World Athletics](link_10).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_men_record-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_women_record-4) The men's world record time is 56:51, set by [Yomif Kejelcha](link_2) in 2026 in [Buenos Aires](link_11). [Jacob Kiplimo](link_12) ran 56:42 in [Barcelona](link_13) in 2025, but this mark was not ratified by World Athletics due to his proximity to the lead car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-5) The women's world record, in a mixed-gender race, is 1:02:52, set by [Letesenbet Gidey](link_4) of Ethiopia in October 2021 in [Valencia, Spain](link_14). The world record for the women's only race is 1:05:15, set by [Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5) of Kenya in September 2026.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-6)

Participation in half marathons has grown steadily since 2003,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) partly because it is a challenging distance, but does not require the same level of training that a marathon does.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) In 2008, _Running USA_ reported that the half marathon was the fastest-growing type of race.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7)

Races close to the official half marathon distance of 21.0975 km (13.1094 mi) have taken place throughout the early 20th century, and athletes have also been timed at the midpoint of full [marathons](link_7). The [1946 Central American and Caribbean Games](link_15) in [Barranquilla](link_16), Colombia featured a road race that is listed at exactly the modern half marathon distance, referred to as the "Carrera Centroamericana y del Caribe: (21 kms. 97,5 metros)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-8) The [1952 South American Championships in Athletics](link_17) in [Buenos Aires](link_11), Argentina featured a road race that was 21.097km, referred to as "la media maratón" ('the half marathon') by the Chilean newspaper _La Nación._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-9)

The earliest half marathon recognised by the [ARRS](link_18) is the 1960 [Romford](link_19) Half Marathon in England, though it was short of the full half marathon distance.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-10) The earliest half marathon recognised by [World Athletics](link_10) is the 1965 [Feckleton Half Marathon](link_20) in England. The event grew in popularity, leading to the eventual establishment of the [World Athletics Road Running Championships](link_21) in 1992, originally titled the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki_Olympic_Stadium "Helsinki Olympic Stadium") where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") is a biennial event which began in [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1983 World Championships in Athletics"). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Athletics_Federations "International Association of Athletics Federations") (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_and_field_athletics "Track and field athletics") events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Championships_in_Athletics#Championships "IAAF World Championships in Athletics"). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usain_Bolt "Usain Bolt") holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Johnson_(sprinter) "Michael Johnson (sprinter)") holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Joyner-Kersee "Jackie Joyner-Kersee") broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_McLaughlin-Levrone "Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone") holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Jackson "Colin Jackson") broke the [110 metre hurdles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/110_metre_hurdles "110 metre hurdles") world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Powell_(long_jumper) "Mike Powell (long jumper)")'s world record [long jump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_jump "Long jump") at the [1991 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1991 World Championships in Athletics") has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Johnson_(sprinter) "Michael Johnson (sprinter)") has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](link_7) has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_15]'s_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

No longer contested at the Summer Olympics

[![Image 3: Usain Bolt in a yellow running vest and green shorts just completing a race](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg/250px-Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg)

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg)

Ethiopian long-distance runner [Kenenisa Bekele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele "Kenenisa Bekele") holds the Olympic record in the 5000 m.

_♦ denotes a performance that is also a current [world record](link_24). Statistics are correct as of August 5, 2024._

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg/250px-Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg)

Russian athlete [Yelena Isinbayeva](link_25) set the Olympic record in the pole vault in Beijing in 2008.

| [World records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics#World_records "List of world records in athletics") |
| Men | ![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg/40px-Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Yomif Kejelcha](link_2)(ETH) 56:51 (2026) |
| Women | **[Mx](link_3)**: ![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg/40px-Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Letesenbet Gidey](link_4)(ETH) 1:02:52 (2021) **[Wo](link_3)**: ![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Flag_of_Kenya.svg/40px-Flag_of_Kenya.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5)(KEN) 1:05:15 (2026) |

A **half marathon** is a [road running](link_6) event of 21.0975 kilometres (c. 13 mi 192.5 yd)—half the distance of a [marathon](link_7).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-1) It is common for a half marathon event to be held concurrently with a marathon or a 5K race, using almost the same course with a late start, an early finish, or shortcuts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-2)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] If finisher medals are awarded, the medal or ribbon may differ from those for the full marathon. The half marathon is also known by its [rounded](link_8) distance: a _21K_, a _21.1K_, or _**13.1** miles_.

A [half marathon world record](link_9) is officially recognised by [World Athletics](link_10).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_men_record-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_women_record-4) The men's world record time is 56:51, set by [Yomif Kejelcha](link_2) in 2026 in [Buenos Aires](link_11). [Jacob Kiplimo](link_12) ran 56:42 in [Barcelona](link_13) in 2025, but this mark was not ratified by World Athletics due to his proximity to the lead car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-5) The women's world record, in a mixed-gender race, is 1:02:52, set by [Letesenbet Gidey](link_4) of Ethiopia in October 2021 in [Valencia, Spain](link_14). The world record for the women's only race is 1:05:15, set by [Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5) of Kenya in September 2026.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-6)

Participation in half marathons has grown steadily since 2003,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) partly because it is a challenging distance, but does not require the same level of training that a marathon does.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) In 2008, _Running USA_ reported that the half marathon was the fastest-growing type of race.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7)

Races close to the official half marathon distance of 21.0975 km (13.1094 mi) have taken place throughout the early 20th century, and athletes have also been timed at the midpoint of full [marathons](link_7). The [1946 Central American and Caribbean Games](link_15) in [Barranquilla](link_16), Colombia featured a road race that is listed at exactly the modern half marathon distance, referred to as the "Carrera Centroamericana y del Caribe: (21 kms. 97,5 metros)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-8) The [1952 South American Championships in Athletics](link_17) in [Buenos Aires](link_11), Argentina featured a road race that was 21.097km, referred to as "la media maratón" ('the half marathon') by the Chilean newspaper _La Nación._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-9)

The earliest half marathon recognised by the [ARRS](link_18) is the 1960 [Romford](link_19) Half Marathon in England, though it was short of the full half marathon distance.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-10) The earliest half marathon recognised by [World Athletics](link_10) is the 1965 [Feckleton Half Marathon](link_20) in England. The event grew in popularity, leading to the eventual establishment of the [World Athletics Road Running Championships](link_21) in 1992, originally titled the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships.

*   Updated 23 August 2026.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-12)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](link_7) has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_15]'s_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

No longer contested at the Summer Olympics

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

Ethiopian long-distance runner [Kenenisa Bekele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele "Kenenisa Bekele") holds the Olympic record in the 5000 m.

| Women | **[Mx](link_3)**: ![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg/40px-Flag_of_Ethiopia.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Letesenbet Gidey](link_4)(ETH) 1:02:52 (2021) **[Wo](link_3)**: ![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Flag_of_Kenya.svg/40px-Flag_of_Kenya.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5)(KEN) 1:05:15 (2026) |

A **half marathon** is a [road running](link_6) event of 21.0975 kilometres (c. 13 mi 192.5 yd)—half the distance of a [marathon](link_7).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-1) It is common for a half marathon event to be held concurrently with a marathon or a 5K race, using almost the same course with a late start, an early finish, or shortcuts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-2)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] If finisher medals are awarded, the medal or ribbon may differ from those for the full marathon. The half marathon is also known by its [rounded](link_8) distance: a _21K_, a _21.1K_, or _**13.1** miles_.

A [half marathon world record](link_9) is officially recognised by [World Athletics](link_10).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_men_record-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-IAAF_women_record-4) The men's world record time is 56:51, set by [Yomif Kejelcha](link_2) in 2026 in [Buenos Aires](link_11). [Jacob Kiplimo](link_12) ran 56:42 in [Barcelona](link_13) in 2025, but this mark was not ratified by World Athletics due to his proximity to the lead car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-5) The women's world record, in a mixed-gender race, is 1:02:52, set by [Letesenbet Gidey](link_4) of Ethiopia in October 2021 in [Valencia, Spain](link_14). The world record for the women's only race is 1:05:15, set by [Agnes Jebet Ngetich](link_5) of Kenya in September 2026.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-6)

Participation in half marathons has grown steadily since 2003,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) partly because it is a challenging distance, but does not require the same level of training that a marathon does.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7) In 2008, _Running USA_ reported that the half marathon was the fastest-growing type of race.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-nytimes-7)

Races close to the official half marathon distance of 21.0975 km (13.1094 mi) have taken place throughout the early 20th century, and athletes have also been timed at the midpoint of full [marathons](link_7). The [1946 Central American and Caribbean Games](link_15) in [Barranquilla](link_16), Colombia featured a road race that is listed at exactly the modern half marathon distance, referred to as the "Carrera Centroamericana y del Caribe: (21 kms. 97,5 metros)".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-8) The [1952 South American Championships in Athletics](link_17) in [Buenos Aires](link_11), Argentina featured a road race that was 21.097km, referred to as "la media maratón" ('the half marathon') by the Chilean newspaper _La Nación._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-9)

The earliest half marathon recognised by the [ARRS](link_18) is the 1960 [Romford](link_19) Half Marathon in England, though it was short of the full half marathon distance.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-10) The earliest half marathon recognised by [World Athletics](link_10) is the 1965 [Feckleton Half Marathon](link_20) in England. The event grew in popularity, leading to the eventual establishment of the [World Athletics Road Running Championships](link_21) in 1992, originally titled the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships.

*   Updated 23 August 2026.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon#cite_note-12)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](link_7) has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_15]'s_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

No longer contested at the Summer Olympics

[![Image 3: Usain Bolt in a yellow running vest and green shorts just completing a race](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg/250px-Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg)

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg)

Ethiopian long-distance runner [Kenenisa Bekele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele "Kenenisa Bekele") holds the Olympic record in the 5000 m.

_♦ denotes a performance that is also a current [world record](link_24). Statistics are correct as of August 5, 2024._

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg/250px-Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg)

Russian athlete [Yelena Isinbayeva](link_25) set the Olympic record in the pole vault in Beijing in 2008.
