From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Violah Jepchumba

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg/250px-Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg)

Personal information

Nationality![Image 2: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain "Bahrain")
Born 16 August 1990 (age 36)

Medal record Women's [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)") Representing ![Image 3: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain "Bahrain") [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games") ![Image 4: Gold medal – first place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg/20px-Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2022 Hangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Asian_Games "2022 Asian Games")[10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2022_Asian_Games_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2022 Asian Games – Women's 10,000 metres") [Islamic Solidarity Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Solidarity_Games "Islamic Solidarity Games") ![Image 5: Silver medal – second place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg/20px-Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2025 Riyadh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Islamic_Solidarity_Games "2025 Islamic Solidarity Games")[10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2025_Islamic_Solidarity_Games "Athletics at the 2025 Islamic Solidarity Games")

**Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio** (born 23 October 1990), also known as **Violah Jepchumba**, is a Kenyan-born Bahraini [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner") who competes in [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") events up to the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance. During her career she has represented both Kenya and Bahrain. She is the current Asian Record holder in the half-marathon (established 1 April 2017) with a winning time of 1:05:22. In 2016, at Praha, she ran a personal best of 1:05:51, which then ranked her as the third fastest woman ever.

She began competing internationally in 2014 and was runner-up in her first European outing at the [Parelloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parelloop "Parelloop"). That year she won a series of lower-level German road races, including the [Paderborner Osterlauf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paderborner_Osterlauf?action=edit&redlink=1 "Paderborner Osterlauf (page does not exist)"), as well as the [Route du Vin Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Route_du_Vin_Half_Marathon "Route du Vin Half Marathon") in Luxembourg. In the 2015 season she improved her half marathon best to 1:11:46 at the [Göteborgsvarvet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%B6teborgsvarvet "Göteborgsvarvet"), was runner-up at the [Kärnten Läuft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%A4rnten_L%C3%A4uft "Kärnten Läuft"), then won the [Udine Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udine_Half_Marathon "Udine Half Marathon") in a new best of 1:09:29.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-ARRS-1)

Jepchumba raised her status with a win at the [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)") in January 2016, beating athletes including world medallists [Helah Kiprop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helah_Kiprop "Helah Kiprop") and [Hyvin Kiyeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyvin_Kiyeng "Hyvin Kiyeng"), and elite marathon runner [Jemima Sumgong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jemima_Sumgong "Jemima Sumgong").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-2) She entered the [Prague Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague_Half_Marathon "Prague Half Marathon") and delivered far beyond expectations with a winning time of 1:05:51. This was the fourth fastest time ever recorded for the distance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-3) Only [Florence Jebet Kiplagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Jebet_Kiplagat "Florence Jebet Kiplagat") and [Mary Jepkosgei Keitany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Jepkosgei_Keitany "Mary Jepkosgei Keitany") had run faster at that point.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-4) She extended her win streak at the [Istanbul Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul_Half_Marathon "Istanbul Half Marathon") later that month.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-5)

In July 2017 Jepchumba transferred her allegiance for athletics events from Kenya to Bahrain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-6)

She tested positive for [erythropoietin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erythropoietin "Erythropoietin") (EPO) in drug tests in August and September 2017 and received a four-year ban for doping.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-7)

Jepchumba won the gold medal in the 10,000m at the [2022 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Asian_Games "2022 Asian Games") in Hangzhou.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-8)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](link_7) has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_15]'s_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Olympic_flag.svg/250px-Olympic_flag.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olympic_flag.svg)

Athletics records in the Summer Olympic Games have been recorded since 1896.

The modern Summer [Olympic Games](link_0) have been held every four years since the first Games in [1896](link_1) (except 1916 due to the First World War, 1940 and 1944 due to the Second World War, and 2020 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](link_2)) and [Olympic records](link_3) are recognised by the [International Olympic Committee](link_4) (IOC) in each event. The [athletics](link_5) events, which take place at each Games, are divided into four groups: [track events](link_6) (including sprints, middle- and long-distance running, hurdling and relays), [field events](link_6) (including javelin, discus, hammer, shot put, pole vault, high, long and triple jumps), road events (such as walks and the marathon) and combined events (the heptathlon and the decathlon).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1) Women compete in 23 athletics events during the Games,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-2) and men compete in 24; while 21 of the events are the same for both men and women, men exclusively compete in the 50 km walk, the women's combined event is the heptathlon while the men compete in the decathlon, and the short distance hurdles for women is contested over 100 m, ten metres shorter than the men's event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-men-1)

Some Olympic records have been broken but later rescinded by the IOC. In [1988](link_7), Canadian sprinter [Ben Johnson](link_8) broke the Olympic and World record in the [100 metres](link_9) sprint, but was subsequently disqualified after it was discovered that he had used [anabolic steroids](link_10) to enhance his performance. His record was expunged and the gold medal was instead awarded to original silver medalist American [Carl Lewis](link_11).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-3) Hungarian athlete [Róbert Fazekas](link_12) broke the Olympic record in the men's discus in [2004](link_13) but was later stripped of both his gold medal and the record after it was deemed that he had "committed an anti-doping rule violation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-5)

The longest standing modern Olympic athletics record is [Bob Beamon](link_14)'s achievement in the men's long jump at the [1968 Summer Olympics](link_15).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-beamon-6) The jump, at 8.90 m (29 ft 2 in), also broke the existing [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_16]'s_long_jump_world_record_progression "Men's long jump world record progression") by 55 cm (22 in), and stood as the world record for 23 years until Beamon's compatriot, [Mike Powell](link_17), jumped farther in the [1991 World Championships in Athletics](link_18) in [Tokyo](link_19).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-7)

Note, only those events currently competed for and recognised by the IOC as Summer Olympic events are listed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics#cite_note-8)

No longer contested at the Summer Olympics

[![Image 3: Usain Bolt in a yellow running vest and green shorts just completing a race](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg/250px-Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Usain_Bolt_Olympics_Celebration.jpg)

[Usain Bolt](link_20) currently holds three Olympic records; two individually in the [100 m](link_9)&[200 m](link_21), and one with the [Jamaican](link_22)[4 × 100 m relay](link_23) team.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg/250px-Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenenisa_Bekele_2014_Paris_Marathon_t084500.jpg)

Ethiopian long-distance runner [Kenenisa Bekele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenenisa_Bekele "Kenenisa Bekele") holds the Olympic record in the 5000 m.

_♦ denotes a performance that is also a current [world record](link_24). Statistics are correct as of August 5, 2024._

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg/250px-Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Isinbayeva_Berlin_2009.jpg)

Russian athlete [Yelena Isinbayeva](link_25) set the Olympic record in the pole vault in Beijing in 2008.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Violah Jepchumba

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg/250px-Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg)
Violah Jepchumba in Prague
Personal information
Full name Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio
Nationality![Image 2: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0)
Born 16 August 1990 (age 36)

[Kenya](link_1)
Sport
Sport[Long-distance running](link_2)
Medal record Women's [athletics](link_3) Representing ![Image 3: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0) [Asian Games](link_4) ![Image 4: Gold medal – first place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg/20px-Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2022 Hangzhou](link_5)[10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2022_Asian_Games_%E2%80%93_Women [link_6]'s_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2022 Asian Games – Women's 10,000 metres") [Islamic Solidarity Games](link_7) ![Image 5: Silver medal – second place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg/20px-Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2025 Riyadh](link_8)[10,000 m](link_9)

**Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio** (born 23 October 1990), also known as **Violah Jepchumba**, is a Kenyan-born Bahraini [long-distance runner](link_10) who competes in [road running](link_11) events up to the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance. During her career she has represented both Kenya and Bahrain. She is the current Asian Record holder in the half-marathon (established 1 April 2017) with a winning time of 1:05:22. In 2016, at Praha, she ran a personal best of 1:05:51, which then ranked her as the third fastest woman ever.

She began competing internationally in 2014 and was runner-up in her first European outing at the [Parelloop](link_12). That year she won a series of lower-level German road races, including the [Paderborner Osterlauf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paderborner_Osterlauf?action=edit&redlink=1 "Paderborner Osterlauf (page does not exist)"), as well as the [Route du Vin Half Marathon](link_13) in Luxembourg. In the 2015 season she improved her half marathon best to 1:11:46 at the [Göteborgsvarvet](link_14), was runner-up at the [Kärnten Läuft](link_15), then won the [Udine Half Marathon](link_16) in a new best of 1:09:29.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-ARRS-1)

Jepchumba raised her status with a win at the [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)") in January 2016, beating athletes including world medallists [Helah Kiprop](link_17) and [Hyvin Kiyeng](link_18), and elite marathon runner [Jemima Sumgong](link_19).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-2) She entered the [Prague Half Marathon](link_20) and delivered far beyond expectations with a winning time of 1:05:51. This was the fourth fastest time ever recorded for the distance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-3) Only [Florence Jebet Kiplagat](link_21) and [Mary Jepkosgei Keitany](link_22) had run faster at that point.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-4) She extended her win streak at the [Istanbul Half Marathon](link_23) later that month.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-5)

In July 2017 Jepchumba transferred her allegiance for athletics events from Kenya to Bahrain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-6)

She tested positive for [erythropoietin](link_24) (EPO) in drug tests in August and September 2017 and received a four-year ban for doping.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-7)

Jepchumba won the gold medal in the 10,000m at the [2022 Asian Games](link_5) in Hangzhou.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-8)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](link_7) has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_15]'s_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Violah Jepchumba

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg/250px-Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg)
Violah Jepchumba in Prague
Personal information
Full name Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio
Nationality![Image 2: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0)
Born 16 August 1990 (age 36)

[Kenya](link_1)
Sport
Sport[Long-distance running](link_2)
Medal record Women's [athletics](link_3) Representing ![Image 3: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0) [Asian Games](link_4) ![Image 4: Gold medal – first place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg/20px-Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2022 Hangzhou](link_5)[10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2022_Asian_Games_%E2%80%93_Women [link_6]'s_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2022 Asian Games – Women's 10,000 metres") [Islamic Solidarity Games](link_7) ![Image 5: Silver medal – second place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg/20px-Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2025 Riyadh](link_8)[10,000 m](link_9)

**Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio** (born 23 October 1990), also known as **Violah Jepchumba**, is a Kenyan-born Bahraini [long-distance runner](link_10) who competes in [road running](link_11) events up to the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance. During her career she has represented both Kenya and Bahrain. She is the current Asian Record holder in the half-marathon (established 1 April 2017) with a winning time of 1:05:22. In 2016, at Praha, she ran a personal best of 1:05:51, which then ranked her as the third fastest woman ever.

She began competing internationally in 2014 and was runner-up in her first European outing at the [Parelloop](link_12). That year she won a series of lower-level German road races, including the [Paderborner Osterlauf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paderborner_Osterlauf?action=edit&redlink=1 "Paderborner Osterlauf (page does not exist)"), as well as the [Route du Vin Half Marathon](link_13) in Luxembourg. In the 2015 season she improved her half marathon best to 1:11:46 at the [Göteborgsvarvet](link_14), was runner-up at the [Kärnten Läuft](link_15), then won the [Udine Half Marathon](link_16) in a new best of 1:09:29.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-ARRS-1)

Jepchumba raised her status with a win at the [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)") in January 2016, beating athletes including world medallists [Helah Kiprop](link_17) and [Hyvin Kiyeng](link_18), and elite marathon runner [Jemima Sumgong](link_19).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-2) She entered the [Prague Half Marathon](link_20) and delivered far beyond expectations with a winning time of 1:05:51. This was the fourth fastest time ever recorded for the distance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-3) Only [Florence Jebet Kiplagat](link_21) and [Mary Jepkosgei Keitany](link_22) had run faster at that point.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-4) She extended her win streak at the [Istanbul Half Marathon](link_23) later that month.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-5)

In July 2017 Jepchumba transferred her allegiance for athletics events from Kenya to Bahrain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-6)

She tested positive for [erythropoietin](link_24) (EPO) in drug tests in August and September 2017 and received a four-year ban for doping.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-7)

Jepchumba won the gold medal in the 10,000m at the [2022 Asian Games](link_5) in Hangzhou.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-8)

*   [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)"): 2016 – 1st place; time (unknown)

*   Casablanca Memorial Rahal 10K: 2015– 1st place; time 32:09

**Marílson Gomes dos Santos** (born 6 August 1977) is a Brazilian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner").

Gomes dos Santos won the 2006 and 2008 [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), becoming the first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") to win the race. He was selected as the best male performer at the 2009 Brazilian national championships after breaking the meet records in both the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") and [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") races. He is the current [South American record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_South_American_records_in_athletics "List of South American records in athletics") holder in both these events with times of 13:19.43 and 27:28.12, respectively.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-5)

He has won [medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medal "Medal") at the [South American Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_American_Cross_Country_Championships "South American Cross Country Championships"), starting with a [silver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_medal "Silver medal") in the junior race in 1996, then taking the [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") in the men's long race in 2000,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-GBR-6) before winning his first championship title in 2008.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-23rdEd-7)

He ran at the [2010 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_London_Marathon "2010 London Marathon") and came close to a personal best time, finishing in 2:08:46 for sixth place behind [Abel Kirui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Kirui "Abel Kirui").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-8) He signed up for the New York Marathon that year and used the [Troféu Brasil de Atletismo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trof%C3%A9u_Brasil_de_Atletismo "Troféu Brasil de Atletismo") (the Brazilian athletics championships) as his preparation, winning the 10,000 m title.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-9) He secured his third career win at the Saint Silvester Race in São Paulo at the end of the year – a record number for a Brazilian runner since the opening of the run for international participant (since 1945).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-10)

At the [2011 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_London_Marathon "2011 London Marathon"), he set a personal best of 2:06:34 hours and placed fourth in the fast race behind a Kenyan trio of [Emmanuel Mutai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Mutai "Emmanuel Mutai"), [Martin Lel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lel "Martin Lel") and [Patrick Makau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Makau "Patrick Makau").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-11)

Gomes dos Santos competed in the marathon at the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon"), [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") Olympics with the best result of fifth place in 2012.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-sr-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-rio-2) He is married to [Juliana Paula dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juliana_Paula_dos_Santos "Juliana Paula dos Santos"), a fellow runner who won gold medals at the 2007 and 2015 Pan American Games. They have a son Miguel, who is also a runner and ran a U-16 national record in the 1000m (2:28) at the Campeonatos Brasileiros Interclubes CBI® de Atletismo Loterias Caixa! **Marílson Gomes dos Santos** (born 6 August 1977) is a Brazilian [long-distance runner](link_18).

Gomes dos Santos won the 2006 and 2008 [New York City Marathon](link_19), becoming the first [South American](link_20) to win the race. He was selected as the best male performer at the 2009 Brazilian national championships after breaking the meet records in both the [5000 metres](link_21) and [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") races. He is the current [South American record](link_22) holder in both these events with times of 13:19.43 and 27:28.12, respectively.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-5)

He has won [medals](link_23) at the [South American Cross Country Championships](link_24), starting with a [silver](link_25) in the junior race in 1996, then taking the [bronze](link_26) in the men's long race in 2000,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-GBR-6) before winning his first championship title in 2008.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-23rdEd-7)

He ran at the [2010 London Marathon](link_27) and came close to a personal best time, finishing in 2:08:46 for sixth place behind [Abel Kirui](link_28).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-8) He signed up for the New York Marathon that year and used the [Troféu Brasil de Atletismo](link_29) (the Brazilian athletics championships) as his preparation, winning the 10,000 m title.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-9) He secured his third career win at the Saint Silvester Race in São Paulo at the end of the year – a record number for a Brazilian runner since the opening of the run for international participant (since 1945).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-10)

At the [2011 London Marathon](link_30), he set a personal best of 2:06:34 hours and placed fourth in the fast race behind a Kenyan trio of [Emmanuel Mutai](link_31), [Martin Lel](link_32) and [Patrick Makau](link_33).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-11)

Gomes dos Santos competed in the marathon at the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_34]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon"), [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_35]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_36]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") Olympics with the best result of fifth place in 2012.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-sr-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-rio-2) He is married to [Juliana Paula dos Santos](link_37), a fellow runner who won gold medals at the 2007 and 2015 Pan American Games. They have a son Miguel, who is also a runner and ran a U-16 national record in the 1000m (2:28) at the Campeonatos Brasileiros Interclubes CBI® de Atletismo Loterias Caixa! [[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-nbc-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](link_7) has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_15]'s_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Violah Jepchumba

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg/250px-Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg)
Violah Jepchumba in Prague
Personal information
Full name Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio
Nationality![Image 2: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0)

**Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio** (born 23 October 1990), also known as **Violah Jepchumba**, is a Kenyan-born Bahraini [long-distance runner](link_10) who competes in [road running](link_11) events up to the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance. During her career she has represented both Kenya and Bahrain. She is the current Asian Record holder in the half-marathon (established 1 April 2017) with a winning time of 1:05:22. In 2016, at Praha, she ran a personal best of 1:05:51, which then ranked her as the third fastest woman ever.

She began competing internationally in 2014 and was runner-up in her first European outing at the [Parelloop](link_12). That year she won a series of lower-level German road races, including the [Paderborner Osterlauf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paderborner_Osterlauf?action=edit&redlink=1 "Paderborner Osterlauf (page does not exist)"), as well as the [Route du Vin Half Marathon](link_13) in Luxembourg. In the 2015 season she improved her half marathon best to 1:11:46 at the [Göteborgsvarvet](link_14), was runner-up at the [Kärnten Läuft](link_15), then won the [Udine Half Marathon](link_16) in a new best of 1:09:29.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-ARRS-1)

Jepchumba raised her status with a win at the [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)") in January 2016, beating athletes including world medallists [Helah Kiprop](link_17) and [Hyvin Kiyeng](link_18), and elite marathon runner [Jemima Sumgong](link_19).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-2) She entered the [Prague Half Marathon](link_20) and delivered far beyond expectations with a winning time of 1:05:51. This was the fourth fastest time ever recorded for the distance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-3) Only [Florence Jebet Kiplagat](link_21) and [Mary Jepkosgei Keitany](link_22) had run faster at that point.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-4) She extended her win streak at the [Istanbul Half Marathon](link_23) later that month.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-5)

In July 2017 Jepchumba transferred her allegiance for athletics events from Kenya to Bahrain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-6)

She tested positive for [erythropoietin](link_24) (EPO) in drug tests in August and September 2017 and received a four-year ban for doping.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-7)

Jepchumba won the gold medal in the 10,000m at the [2022 Asian Games](link_5) in Hangzhou.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-8)

**Marílson Gomes dos Santos** (born 6 August 1977) is a Brazilian [long-distance runner](link_18).

Gomes dos Santos won the 2006 and 2008 [New York City Marathon](link_19), becoming the first [South American](link_20) to win the race. He was selected as the best male performer at the 2009 Brazilian national championships after breaking the meet records in both the [5000 metres](link_21) and [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") races. He is the current [South American record](link_22) holder in both these events with times of 13:19.43 and 27:28.12, respectively.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-5)

He has won [medals](link_23) at the [South American Cross Country Championships](link_24), starting with a [silver](link_25) in the junior race in 1996, then taking the [bronze](link_26) in the men's long race in 2000,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-GBR-6) before winning his first championship title in 2008.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-23rdEd-7)

He ran at the [2010 London Marathon](link_27) and came close to a personal best time, finishing in 2:08:46 for sixth place behind [Abel Kirui](link_28).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-8) He signed up for the New York Marathon that year and used the [Troféu Brasil de Atletismo](link_29) (the Brazilian athletics championships) as his preparation, winning the 10,000 m title.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-9) He secured his third career win at the Saint Silvester Race in São Paulo at the end of the year – a record number for a Brazilian runner since the opening of the run for international participant (since 1945).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-10)

At the [2011 London Marathon](link_30), he set a personal best of 2:06:34 hours and placed fourth in the fast race behind a Kenyan trio of [Emmanuel Mutai](link_31), [Martin Lel](link_32) and [Patrick Makau](link_33).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-11)

Gomes dos Santos competed in the marathon at the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_34]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon"), [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_35]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_36]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") Olympics with the best result of fifth place in 2012.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-sr-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-rio-2) He is married to [Juliana Paula dos Santos](link_37), a fellow runner who won gold medals at the 2007 and 2015 Pan American Games. They have a son Miguel, who is also a runner and ran a U-16 national record in the 1000m (2:28) at the Campeonatos Brasileiros Interclubes CBI® de Atletismo Loterias Caixa! [[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-nbc-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

Double record holder [Michael Johnson](link_7) has held the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men [link_15]'s_400_metres_world_record_progression "Men's 400 metres world record progression") world championships record with his run in Seville for over 25 years.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Violah Jepchumba

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg/250px-Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg)
Violah Jepchumba in Prague
Personal information
Full name Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio
Nationality![Image 2: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0)
Born 16 August 1990 (age 36)

[Kenya](link_1)
Sport
Sport[Long-distance running](link_2)
Medal record Women's [athletics](link_3) Representing ![Image 3: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0) [Asian Games](link_4) ![Image 4: Gold medal – first place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg/20px-Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2022 Hangzhou](link_5)[10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2022_Asian_Games_%E2%80%93_Women [link_6]'s_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2022 Asian Games – Women's 10,000 metres") [Islamic Solidarity Games](link_7) ![Image 5: Silver medal – second place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg/20px-Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2025 Riyadh](link_8)[10,000 m](link_9)

**Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio** (born 23 October 1990), also known as **Violah Jepchumba**, is a Kenyan-born Bahraini [long-distance runner](link_10) who competes in [road running](link_11) events up to the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance. During her career she has represented both Kenya and Bahrain. She is the current Asian Record holder in the half-marathon (established 1 April 2017) with a winning time of 1:05:22. In 2016, at Praha, she ran a personal best of 1:05:51, which then ranked her as the third fastest woman ever.

She began competing internationally in 2014 and was runner-up in her first European outing at the [Parelloop](link_12). That year she won a series of lower-level German road races, including the [Paderborner Osterlauf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paderborner_Osterlauf?action=edit&redlink=1 "Paderborner Osterlauf (page does not exist)"), as well as the [Route du Vin Half Marathon](link_13) in Luxembourg. In the 2015 season she improved her half marathon best to 1:11:46 at the [Göteborgsvarvet](link_14), was runner-up at the [Kärnten Läuft](link_15), then won the [Udine Half Marathon](link_16) in a new best of 1:09:29.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-ARRS-1)

Jepchumba raised her status with a win at the [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)") in January 2016, beating athletes including world medallists [Helah Kiprop](link_17) and [Hyvin Kiyeng](link_18), and elite marathon runner [Jemima Sumgong](link_19).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-2) She entered the [Prague Half Marathon](link_20) and delivered far beyond expectations with a winning time of 1:05:51. This was the fourth fastest time ever recorded for the distance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-3) Only [Florence Jebet Kiplagat](link_21) and [Mary Jepkosgei Keitany](link_22) had run faster at that point.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-4) She extended her win streak at the [Istanbul Half Marathon](link_23) later that month.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-5)

In July 2017 Jepchumba transferred her allegiance for athletics events from Kenya to Bahrain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-6)

She tested positive for [erythropoietin](link_24) (EPO) in drug tests in August and September 2017 and received a four-year ban for doping.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-7)

Jepchumba won the gold medal in the 10,000m at the [2022 Asian Games](link_5) in Hangzhou.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-8)

*   [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)"): 2016 – 1st place; time (unknown)

*   Laayoune Half Marathon: 2015 – 1st place; time 1:12:35
*   Casablanca Memorial Rahal 10K: 2015– 1st place; time 32:09

**Marílson Gomes dos Santos** (born 6 August 1977) is a Brazilian [long-distance runner](link_18).

Gomes dos Santos won the 2006 and 2008 [New York City Marathon](link_19), becoming the first [South American](link_20) to win the race. He was selected as the best male performer at the 2009 Brazilian national championships after breaking the meet records in both the [5000 metres](link_21) and [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") races. He is the current [South American record](link_22) holder in both these events with times of 13:19.43 and 27:28.12, respectively.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-5)

He has won [medals](link_23) at the [South American Cross Country Championships](link_24), starting with a [silver](link_25) in the junior race in 1996, then taking the [bronze](link_26) in the men's long race in 2000,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-GBR-6) before winning his first championship title in 2008.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-23rdEd-7)

He ran at the [2010 London Marathon](link_27) and came close to a personal best time, finishing in 2:08:46 for sixth place behind [Abel Kirui](link_28).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-8) He signed up for the New York Marathon that year and used the [Troféu Brasil de Atletismo](link_29) (the Brazilian athletics championships) as his preparation, winning the 10,000 m title.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-9) He secured his third career win at the Saint Silvester Race in São Paulo at the end of the year – a record number for a Brazilian runner since the opening of the run for international participant (since 1945).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-10)

At the [2011 London Marathon](link_30), he set a personal best of 2:06:34 hours and placed fourth in the fast race behind a Kenyan trio of [Emmanuel Mutai](link_31), [Martin Lel](link_32) and [Patrick Makau](link_33).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-11)

Gomes dos Santos competed in the marathon at the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_34]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon"), [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_35]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_36]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") Olympics with the best result of fifth place in 2012.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-sr-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-rio-2) He is married to [Juliana Paula dos Santos](link_37), a fellow runner who won gold medals at the 2007 and 2015 Pan American Games. They have a son Miguel, who is also a runner and ran a U-16 national record in the 1000m (2:28) at the Campeonatos Brasileiros Interclubes CBI® de Atletismo Loterias Caixa! [[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-nbc-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg/250px-200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:200metres_Helsinki2005.jpg)

Athletes competing at the [Helsinki Olympic Stadium](link_0) where the first and tenth editions of the Championships were staged.

The [World Athletics Championships](link_1) is a biennial event which began in [1983](link_2). Organised by the [International Association of Athletics Federations](link_3) (IAAF), the World Championships are a competition comprising [track and field athletics](link_4) events available to male and female athletes from any of the IAAF's 213 member federations. Championship records are set when an athlete achieves the best mark in an event at one of the [editions of the Championships](link_5). World, area, and national records have been set at the championships over the course of its history.

Competitors at the World Championships come from around the globe and records have been broken by athletes from all six continents. The United States has been the most successful competitor at the World Championships in both medals and records.

Four athletes hold multiple records:

*   [Usain Bolt](link_6) holds records in the 100 and 200 metres as well as the 4 × 100 relay
*   [Michael Johnson](link_7) holds individual and relay records in the 400 metres
*   [Jackie Joyner-Kersee](link_8) broke both the heptathlon and long jump records
*   [Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone](link_9) holds records in the 400 meters, 400 metres hurdles as well as the 4 × 400 relay

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Colin_Jackson.jpg/250px-Colin_Jackson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colin_Jackson.jpg)

[Colin Jackson](link_10) broke the [110 metre hurdles](link_11) world record in 1993; a record which stood for over a decade.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg/250px-Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Osaka07_D7A_Mike_Powell.jpg)

[Mike Powell](link_12)'s world record [long jump](link_13) at the [1991 Championships](link_14) has never been bettered.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg/250px-Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Johnson_Sydney2000.jpg)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Violah Jepchumba

[![Image 1](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg/250px-Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Violah_Jepchumba_in_Prague.jpg)
Violah Jepchumba in Prague
Personal information
Full name Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio
Nationality![Image 2: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0)
Born 16 August 1990 (age 36)

Sport[Long-distance running](link_2)
Medal record Women's [athletics](link_3) Representing ![Image 3: Stub icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Flag_of_Bahrain.svg/40px-Flag_of_Bahrain.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Bahrain](link_0) [Asian Games](link_4) ![Image 4: Gold medal – first place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg/20px-Gold_medal_icon_%28G_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2022 Hangzhou](link_5)[10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2022_Asian_Games_%E2%80%93_Women [link_6]'s_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2022 Asian Games – Women's 10,000 metres") [Islamic Solidarity Games](link_7) ![Image 5: Silver medal – second place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg/20px-Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2025 Riyadh](link_8)[10,000 m](link_9)

**Violah Jepchumba Kilonzo Motosio** (born 23 October 1990), also known as **Violah Jepchumba**, is a Kenyan-born Bahraini [long-distance runner](link_10) who competes in [road running](link_11) events up to the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance. During her career she has represented both Kenya and Bahrain. She is the current Asian Record holder in the half-marathon (established 1 April 2017) with a winning time of 1:05:22. In 2016, at Praha, she ran a personal best of 1:05:51, which then ranked her as the third fastest woman ever.

She began competing internationally in 2014 and was runner-up in her first European outing at the [Parelloop](link_12). That year she won a series of lower-level German road races, including the [Paderborner Osterlauf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paderborner_Osterlauf?action=edit&redlink=1 "Paderborner Osterlauf (page does not exist)"), as well as the [Route du Vin Half Marathon](link_13) in Luxembourg. In the 2015 season she improved her half marathon best to 1:11:46 at the [Göteborgsvarvet](link_14), was runner-up at the [Kärnten Läuft](link_15), then won the [Udine Half Marathon](link_16) in a new best of 1:09:29.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-ARRS-1)

Jepchumba raised her status with a win at the [Discovery Kenya Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Kenya_Cross_Country?action=edit&redlink=1 "Discovery Kenya Cross Country (page does not exist)") in January 2016, beating athletes including world medallists [Helah Kiprop](link_17) and [Hyvin Kiyeng](link_18), and elite marathon runner [Jemima Sumgong](link_19).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-2) She entered the [Prague Half Marathon](link_20) and delivered far beyond expectations with a winning time of 1:05:51. This was the fourth fastest time ever recorded for the distance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-3) Only [Florence Jebet Kiplagat](link_21) and [Mary Jepkosgei Keitany](link_22) had run faster at that point.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-4) She extended her win streak at the [Istanbul Half Marathon](link_23) later that month.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-5)

In July 2017 Jepchumba transferred her allegiance for athletics events from Kenya to Bahrain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-6)

She tested positive for [erythropoietin](link_24) (EPO) in drug tests in August and September 2017 and received a four-year ban for doping.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-7)

Jepchumba won the gold medal in the 10,000m at the [2022 Asian Games](link_5) in Hangzhou.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violah_Jepchumba#cite_note-8)

Dos Santos in 2006

**Marílson Gomes dos Santos** (born 6 August 1977) is a Brazilian [long-distance runner](link_18).

Gomes dos Santos won the 2006 and 2008 [New York City Marathon](link_19), becoming the first [South American](link_20) to win the race. He was selected as the best male performer at the 2009 Brazilian national championships after breaking the meet records in both the [5000 metres](link_21) and [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") races. He is the current [South American record](link_22) holder in both these events with times of 13:19.43 and 27:28.12, respectively.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-5)

He has won [medals](link_23) at the [South American Cross Country Championships](link_24), starting with a [silver](link_25) in the junior race in 1996, then taking the [bronze](link_26) in the men's long race in 2000,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-GBR-6) before winning his first championship title in 2008.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-23rdEd-7)

He ran at the [2010 London Marathon](link_27) and came close to a personal best time, finishing in 2:08:46 for sixth place behind [Abel Kirui](link_28).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-8) He signed up for the New York Marathon that year and used the [Troféu Brasil de Atletismo](link_29) (the Brazilian athletics championships) as his preparation, winning the 10,000 m title.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-9) He secured his third career win at the Saint Silvester Race in São Paulo at the end of the year – a record number for a Brazilian runner since the opening of the run for international participant (since 1945).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-10)

At the [2011 London Marathon](link_30), he set a personal best of 2:06:34 hours and placed fourth in the fast race behind a Kenyan trio of [Emmanuel Mutai](link_31), [Martin Lel](link_32) and [Patrick Makau](link_33).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-11)

Gomes dos Santos competed in the marathon at the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_34]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon"), [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_35]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_36]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") Olympics with the best result of fifth place in 2012.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-sr-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar%C3%ADlson_Gomes_dos_Santos#cite_note-rio-2) He is married to [Juliana Paula dos Santos](link_37), a fellow runner who won gold medals at the 2007 and 2015 Pan American Games. They have a son Miguel, who is also a runner and ran a U-16 national record in the 1000m (2:28) at the Campeonatos Brasileiros Interclubes CBI® de Atletismo Loterias Caixa!
